articles.title: Pat Cummins press conference live updates: Australian cricket captain speaks about Usman Khawaja’s ‘sandpapergate’ claims
articles.summary: Cummins speaks about allegations in Usman Khawaja’s book about the 2018 ball-tampering incident. ‘Complete and utter nonsense’: Australia captain Pat Cummins hits back at Khawaja ‘sandpapergate’ claims.
body: He says that I and others were architects of a scheme to ball-tamper with sandpaper. That’s complete and utter nonsense.
Cummins goes on to say he believes Khawaja’s book has “been casual with my [life] and the lives of many others, and I think Australian cricket”.

Another issue addressed in Cummins’s press conference – he took questions for more than an hour – was the punishment handed down to the three players Cricket Australia’s investigation found were responsible for bringing sandpaper onto the field: Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft.

Cummins said he believed the punishments handed down in the wake of the scandal were “way over the top”. Smith and Warner were handed one-year bans, Bancroft (while the player who carried the sandpaper on to the field, he was the most junior of the three) received a nine-month ban.

articles.title: Police decide not to charge Sydney Swans players over incident in Melbourne hotel
articles.summary: Victoria police will not lay charges due to ‘insufficient evidence’ Heeney, Warner, Blakey and Jordon had been under investigation. Victoria police have decided not to charge four Sydney Swans players who were under investigation over an alleged sexual assault at a Melbourne hotel earlier this…
body: Sydney vice-captain Isaac Heeney as well as James Jordon, Chad Warner and Nick Blakey – the latter now a North Melbourne player – are understood to have assisted police with their investigation but will have no further case to answer.
“Following a thorough investigation and based on legal advice, Victoria Police will not proceed with criminal charges due to insufficient evidence,” a police statement read.
“Due to the ongoing civil matter, Victoria Police is unable to make further comment.”

The quartet, along with teammate Riley Bice, were suspended by the Swans in August for breaching the club’s standards, including drinking and bringing women back to their hotel the night after an AFL game in Melbourne.

articles.title: 'Wrong' and 'nonsense' - Cummins on Khawaja sandpaper claims
articles.summary: Australia captain Pat Cummins hits back at former team-mate Usman Khawaja’s claims over the sandpaper scandal, calling them “100% wrong” and “utter nonsense”.
body: In 2018, Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft were punished for a plot to tamper with the ball using sandpaper in Australia's Test against South Africa in Cape Town.

Khawaja has published his autobiography this week and the former batter has said the entire Australia team, which included Cummins, knew about the sandpaper scheme and should have taken responsibility.
But in an extraordinary address to the media in Sydney, Cummins countered and said: "When he says we all knew, if by that he means we knew sandpaper was going out on the field, he's 100% wrong.
"I said that consistently for the last eight years. I did not know that was happening.

articles.title: Australia Test captain Pat Cummins calls Khawaja's sandpapergate claims ‘complete and utter nonsense’
articles.summary: Cummins insists he did not know of ball tampering plot in South Africa. ‘No masterplan around using illegal methods,’ Cummins says. Pat Cummins press conference – live reaction.
body: Pat Cummins has flatly denied Usman Khawaja’s claims that the entire team was implicated in the 2018 sandpaper scandal as “complete and utter nonsense” and “100% wrong” in a defiant appearance at a press conference a week after the allegations came to light.

Appearing before dozens of reporters and cameras at Cricket NSW’s headquarters in Sydney, Cummins refuted the allegations aired in his former teammate’s book, Sabr, and said he had no knowledge of the ball tampering plot in South Africa.

Australia’s captain at the time Steve Smith, vice-captain David Warner and opener Cameron Bancroft were handed long suspensions by Cricket Australia after the governing body’s short investigation into the incident. Khawaja alleges in his memoir that more than just the three banned players were aware of the team’s ball-tampering plans, and that sandpaper was also used on the ball during the preceding Test. The former Australia batter has called for “all” of the team to take collective responsibility.

articles.title: Morgan Rogers says ‘it’s a lie’ that Cole Palmer does not want to play for England
articles.summary: Forward springs to defence of Chelsea teammate. ‘He wanted to come and represent his country’ Morgan Rogers has said accusations that his Chelsea teammate Cole Palmer is not committed to playing for England are “a lie”.
body: Palmer, who was left out of the squad for this week’s Nations League ties against Croatia and Spain, has faced questions over his desire to play international football since withdrawing from last month’s camp with a groin injury. Thomas Tuchel, who did not take the 24-year-old to last summer’s World Cup, expressed irritation at the time, saying the Chelsea attacker “misses too many opportunities” to play for his country.

Tuchel last week insisted Palmer’s latest exclusion was “not personal” but he has placed plenty of store in players showing up to camp. The German has previously said it was “hard to argue” when it was put to him that Palmer does not want to play for the national team after his fourth withdrawal from a squad. But Rogers, who scored in England’s 2-1 win over Croatia on Thursday, delivered a strong rebuttal to claims his friend and teammate is not dedicated to the national team.
“It’s a lie,” Rogers said. “He wants to be here. He wanted to get called up and he wanted to come and represent his country as he always has done. People just see it as news and say the easy thing.

articles.summary: Australia Test captain Pat Cummins dismissed his former team-mate Usman Khawaja's claims as "utter nonsense" after the recently retired batter said in his autobiography that the whole side were aware of ball-tampering that took place on their 2018 tour of South Africa.
body: Khawaja made the revelations in his new book 'Sabr', which was released earlier this week, bringing the scandal back onto the agenda eight years after Cameron Bancroft was caught on camera using sandpaper on the ball while Australia were fielding.

Only Bancroft, then-captain Steve Smith and his vice-captain David Warner were punished, with each receiving lengthy bans as the rest of the Australian team and coaching staff denied knowledge of the scheme.

Cummins, who was a relatively junior member of the side playing in just his 13th Test match, in 2021 issued a joint-statement with fellow bowlers from the fixture Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc and Nathan Lyon, in which they denied knowing that a foreign substance had been taken onto the field to alter the ball in order to try to make it swing.

articles.title: Gauff battles through back injury to keep WTA Finals hopes alive
articles.summary: Coco Gauff shows all of her battling qualities as she fights through a back injury to beat Marta Kostyuk and keep her WTA Finals last-four hopes alive.
body: American Gauff was visibly in pain as she received treatment on her lower back midway through a match she needed to win to stay in the tournament.
She found herself 5-1 down in the second set - only to win six games in a row to complete a 6-4 7-5 win at Indian Wells.
"Physically, I wasn't at my best, which I'm not really used to," Gauff told Sky Sports.
"It was like a mental challenge, learning how to play through that."

articles.title: Korda two shots off lead on return at The Annika as Woad also starts well
articles.summary: World No 1 Nelly Korda made an impressive return to LPGA Tour action after a two-month absence to finish the opening round of The Annika within two shots of the lead.
body: Korda, whose last competitive golf came at the Solheim Cup in September after her most recent LPGA Tour outing in August, shot a bogey-free seven-under par round of 63 at Pelican Golf Club in Florida.
Korda trails Japan's Minami Katsu and Korean Hye-Jin Choi by two shots, with fellow American Lindy Duncan also ahead of her on eight under after making a hole-in-one during her 62.
"It was nice to kind of feel those juices flowing again, especially playing with Hye-Jin who just had a great round today," Korda said.
She already has clinched LPGA player of the year based on points, and Korda can qualify for the LPGA Hall of Fame with a victory in one of the final two events of the season.

articles.title: Ghana kick-start Afcon 2027 bid despite Ayew penalty miss
articles.summary: Ghana kick-start their Afcon 2027 qualifying campaign despite Jordan Ayew having a penalty saved, while Cameroon, Ivory Coast and Senegal register wins.
body: Ghana belatedly kick-started their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) qualifying campaign with a 2-0 home win over Somalia.

Ghana women's coach Kim Bjorkegren was placed in interim charge for this month's double-header against the Ocean Stars, with the West Africans in danger of missing a second successive edition of the Afcon finals.

The hosts were given a chance to take an early lead in Sekondi-Takoradi after Alidu Seidu was pulled down in the box, but Jordan Ayew's 14th-minute penalty was saved by Somalia goalkeeper Ibrahim Hussein.
Ghana did go ahead in first-half stoppage time when Mohammed Salisu headed Mohammed Kudus's deep corner back across goal and Jonas Adjetey nodded in from six yards out.

articles.title: SFA in talks with Boston officials over biennial friendly match
articles.summary: Discussions take place between Scottish football governing's body and a delegation of state senators to build on bonds forged during the World Cup.
body: BBC Scotland has learned that the SFA is in active discussions aimed at a biennial friendly match being held in Boston.

Scotland played two World Cup matches in the US city during the summer and now the governing body and the state of Massachusetts are in talks aimed at building the bonds made between locals and the Tartan Army, through football.
More discussions are due to take place between the SFA and a delegation of state senators ahead of Scotland's Nations League match against North Macedonia at Hampden on Friday.
It has not yet been decided who will play in the game but BBC Scotland understands it will involve the Scoland national team.

articles.title: Pochettino agrees two-and-a-half-year deal to become Man Utd boss
articles.summary: Manchester United and Mauricio Pochettino have agreed a deal for him to become the club's next head coach.
body: Pochettino is expected to sign a two-and-half-year contract at Old Trafford, replacing Michael Carrick, who was sacked earlier on Thursday.
Pochettino - who had a £7m release clause in his USA contract - will take charge of United after overseeing the USA's games against Haiti on Saturday and Wednesday.
The formal announcement of Pochettino's appointed is expected on Friday, with the Argentine set to be United's eighth permanent appointment since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013.
Pochettino's first game in charge will be the trip to Anfield to face Liverpool on November 22, live on Sky Sports.

articles.title: Kansas City Chiefs Reacts to George Karlaftis’ Defensive Performance Against New York Jets
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs celebrated George Karlaftis’ standout defensive performance after their 35-12 victory over the New York Jets, highlighting the edge rusher’s impact on social media.
body: Karlaftis finished with six tackles, including four solo stops, two sacks and a pass breakup. He also recorded three tackles for loss, repeatedly disrupting the Jets’ offense and helping Kansas City turn a difficult opening stretch into a convincing win. His production made him one of the most influential players on the defensive side.

The performance came as the Chiefs sought to rebound from consecutive losses and reestablish their defensive identity. Kansas City recorded five sacks overall, with Chris Jones also collecting two, while Ashton Gillotte added another. The pressure limited New York quarterback Geno Smith and prevented the Jets from building on their early momentum.

After allowing a long scoring drive on the opening possession, the defense tightened considerably. New York managed only 165 total yards for the rest of the game and failed to score in the second half. The Jets were held to minus-13 net yards in the third quarter, underscoring how thoroughly the Chiefs controlled the line of scrimmage after halftime.
Karlaftis’ performance on the defensive end drew the attention of his team. This can be seen in a post Kansas City made on Instagram.
